question: Which of the following is INCORRECT in respect of geostationary satellite?

options.text: Rotate with speed and direction of earth
Orbits are used for IRS satellite
Many of these satellite orbits are also sun-synchronous

solution:
The correct answer is __**Many of these satellite orbits are also sun-synchronou**__s [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Geostationary satellites orbit the Earth in such a way that they remain fixed over one point on the equator.
 
• They are not sun-synchronous, which refers to satellites that maintain a constant angle with the Sun, typically in lower orbits, like those used for Earth observation.
 
• Geostationary satellites must orbit the Earth at an altitude of about **35,786 km (approximately 36,000 km)** above the equator.
 
• This specific altitude allows them to match the Earth's rotational period and stay fixed over one spot.
 
• Geostationary satellites orbit the Earth at the same rotational speed as the Earth (once every 24 hours) and in the same direction, allowing them to remain fixed over a specific point on the Earth's equator.
